exposure: Laparoscopic surgical removal technique for cesarean scar pregnancy
Temporary uterine artery ligation using removable clips
Double layer suture on anterior uterine wall
outcome: Successful removal of cesarean scar pregnancy
cohort: A single woman referred for a suspected type 2 cesarean scar pregnancy at 9 weeks gestation, who had previously undergone unsuccessful ultrasound-guided aspiration, curettage, and methotrexate injection.
finding: Laparoscopic surgical management, incorporating retroperitoneal dissection and vascular control, is a very effective and safe surgical approach to remove a cesarean scar pregnancy.
mod_finding: The study focuses on the management of a cesarean scar pregnancy, which is a complication specifically arising from a prior cesarean delivery.
followup_time: N/A (The study describes the surgical technique and its immediate effectiveness for a pregnancy complication, not a birth; no specific post-surgical follow-up duration for the demonstrated technique's outcome is stated.)
gest_age: 9 weeks gestation (at initial diagnosis of CSP)
